content:
Google Health app was first launched in May alongside the new affordable Google Fitbit Air health tracker series.

Google Health initially only supported one-way Apple Health integration. The app could read and import health data recorded by iPhone, Apple Watch, and other HealthKit-connected apps, but could not write Fitbit data back to Apple Health.

Today's update to the Google Health iOS app fills in the missing other end of the connection.

Google Health can now not only read data from HealthKit, but also write data to Apple Health.

The version 5.05 release notes particularly highlight the Apple Health sync feature:

Workout records, sleep status, vital signs, step count and other Fitbit data can now be shared with other HealthKit-compatible apps according to the permissions set by the user.

Before this year, users who wanted to import Fitbit data into Apple Health generally had to use third-party sync tools or connect indirectly through other services.

This gap can be traced back to 2014. Shortly after Apple introduced HealthKit in iOS 8, Fitbit said it had no plans to support the platform.

Version 5.05 also added the Smart Health Links feature, allowing users to share medical records with healthcare professionals or family members.

The new version of the Google Health iOS app is now available on the App Store. To learn more about Google Health, please visit 9to5Google.
